name: crash-cut-transcripts
description: Every commit path's media operations in their normative order, and the states a reboot after a cut before, during or after any of them may produce. A cut is enumerated at three positions per operation: before it reaches the card, during it (a write tears the program page it was programming; a sync commits an arbitrary subset), and after it returns.

transcripts.name: checkpoint-compaction
transcripts.description: Compaction streams the inactive checkpoint's body a sector at a time and gates it completely before the new epoch's first record exists.
transcripts.note: The body is 127 separate 512-byte sector writes, which is section 6.3's forward pass rather than a buffered materialization: the store stages one entry and one sector, takes each card-resident field from the RAM index, from a journal-carried entry through the per-head slot reference, or from the active checkpoint, and accumulates the body CRC as it goes. One correction to section 6.3's own arithmetic: it calls 208 bytes the largest entry shape, but section 5.1 gives the update-handoff projection 240, so the entry stage is 240 bytes and the whole staging bound is 752.

transcripts.name: ride-checkpoint
transcripts.description: One ride checkpoint: payload first, then the ring slot at sequence mod 16.
transcripts.note: A ride payload is smaller than one 16,384-byte program page, so a cut during its write tears the whole file and the ride restarts at zero. Section 1.1 caps that at one checkpoint interval and calls it not a store fault. Whatever recovery resumes from, the durable bytes must back its finalized prefix CRC.

transcripts.name: generation-seal
transcripts.description: One restart-only upload: the payload is streamed and synchronized, then the sealed WORK slot — the one durable work fact both device profiles write — is gated.
transcripts.note: The payload write's length is the object's, not a fixed record size, so it appears with length zero here. No streaming slot is ever written: this profile acknowledges no offset, so the two payload operations and the six of the gated slot are the whole sequence.

steps.note: the whole payload, streamed from offset zero; the restart-only profile acknowledges none of it
the payload bytes and the length its directory entry records are durable

no slot claims an offset over the payload at any point of this sequence
the sealed body, with a zeroed gate sector and pad
the body is durable
the O2WG gate
seal is durable and domain validation may run

admissibleOutcomes: a claimed generation with no durable work slot, which recovery classifies as restartable work at offset zero
the sealed WORK slot, whose finalized prefix CRC the durable payload backs

transcripts.name: generation-restart
transcripts.description: A readmission rewinding a claimed generation to offset zero. The truncation is synchronized before a byte is accepted again.
transcripts.note: Section 7's restart durability point is satisfied vacuously under the restart-only profile: no WORK slot records a streaming offset, so no truncation can make a recorded prefix unverifiable. The ordering is still the resumable profile's, minus the slot it would write first.

steps.note: truncate the claimed generation to zero
the rewind is durable; only now may a byte be accepted at offset zero
the restreamed payload, from offset zero under the same GenerationId

admissibleOutcomes: the old durable prefix, when the truncation never reached the card
an empty payload, ready to be streamed from offset zero

transcripts.name: lease-recovery-clear
transcripts.description: The bounded recovery suffix that clears every durable live-lease reason before garbage collection may treat any generation as unreachable.
transcripts.note: At most eight such records exist, which is the retention capacity, and section 6.3 counts them into the 55-record recovery suffix. A cut leaves a prefix that a later mount finishes; clearing the bit only in RAM is the fault this sequence exists to forbid.

steps.note: the first retention record, clearing one entry's live-lease bit
its body
its gate
that entry's durable lease reason is gone
the second retention record
its body
its gate
no retained entry carries a lease reason; garbage collection may now run

admissibleOutcomes: no record: every entry still carries its lease reason and the next mount owes the whole suffix
the first entry cleared and the second still owed
no retained entry carrying a lease reason

transcripts.name: short-write
transcripts.description: A write the medium truncates. The writer checks the returned length and abandons the commit.
transcripts.note: One step, because the sequence stops there: the length check fails and nothing after it runs. There are no cut points to enumerate — the fault is the write's own return value.

steps.note: the body stride, of which the medium accepts fewer bytes

admissibleOutcomes: the projection before the record; a short write is an error, never a success

transcripts.name: media-full
transcripts.description: A write the medium refuses for want of space.
transcripts.note: One step, for the same reason as the short write: the refusal ends the sequence.

steps.note: the body stride, which the medium refuses outright

transcripts.name: corrupt-read
transcripts.description: An ordinary commit, followed by a mount whose reads are poisoned one at a time.
transcripts.note: The fault here is on the read path, not the write path, so the steps are an ordinary append and the injection happens during recovery. A corrupt read can cost visibility; it can never invent state.

steps.note: an ordinary append, completed before the fault
its body
its gate
the commit point; the fault is injected into a later *read*

admissibleOutcomes: no checkpoint at all, when the poisoned read was the only valid checkpoint's
